title: A2CN Offer / Counteroffer
description: The Section 7.1 protocol act that carries terms: message_type "offer" in round 1 and "counteroffer" in rounds 2 and beyond. The message object and the terms object stay open, so deal-type terms extensions (spec/schemas/terms/) and vendor fields pass through. The one place this schema closes is the spelling of a line item's two money figures.

message_type.description: "offer" for round 1, "counteroffer" for rounds 2 and beyond (Section 7.1)

in_reply_to.description: The message_id of the most recent offer or counteroffer received from the other party. REQUIRED after round 1, and absent in round 1 (Section 7.1).

sender_verification_method.description: DID URL of the verification method used to sign this message (Section 7.1)

expires_at.description: MUST be after timestamp and MUST NOT exceed timestamp plus the session's round_timeout_seconds (Section 7.1)

terms.description: Section 7.2. Open on purpose: a deal type adds its own members here (spec/schemas/terms/goods_procurement.schema.json, spec/schemas/terms/saas_renewal.schema.json), and the TransactionRecord carries this object unchanged as agreed_terms.

total_value.description: Total monetary value in the smallest unit of terms.currency (Section 7.2)

currency.description: MUST equal the session's negotiated currency; a difference is SESSION_PARAM_CHANGED (Section 7.2)

basis.description: The money basis of the offer's amounts. Present exactly when the session fixed a basis (Sections 6.3.1, 7.2); no other value is valid, including null.

line_items.description: Optional. When present, every entry is a priced line stating its money in integer minor units (Section 7.2).

items.description: A priced line. Its two money figures are integer MINOR units of terms.currency: unit_price_minor and total_minor, both REQUIRED. The bare names unit_price and total are refused by propertyNames rather than simply left undeclared, because this object stays OPEN — a deal type extends it (goods_procurement adds manufacturer_part_number, internal_part_number and unit_of_measure) and a blanket additionalProperties:false would reject those extensions too. The refusal is by name because the two conventions differ by a factor of one hundred: a receiver that read a bare unit_price as minor units, or a pinned unit_price_minor as major units, would agree with the sender about the number and disagree about the amount, and nothing in the message would say so.

quantity.description: A whole number of the stated unit, and never negative: a refund is a negative price, not a negative count. For fractional quantities, use the appropriate smaller unit and say so in unit (Section 7.2).

unit_of_measure.description: Line-item UOM code (e.g. EA, KG). goods_procurement deal-type extension.

unit_price_minor.description: Price of one unit, in integer minor units of terms.currency. An integer VALUE, not a particular spelling: RFC 8785 makes 36000 and 36000.0 the same number and both are valid, while a value with a fractional part is not, and neither is a decimal string or a boolean. Bounded by the safe-integer range, past which a double cannot separate adjacent integers and two implementations could read one document as two different amounts.

total_minor.description: This line's total, in integer minor units of terms.currency, an integer value on the same terms as unit_price_minor.

propertyNames.description: unit_price and total are the bare spellings this schema pins out. State the amounts as unit_price_minor and total_minor.
